A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DReST study and contain readable main text, equations, figures, references, and Appendices A–E. Text comparison and visual inspection support a reliable comparison despite pagination changes.

before.justification: v4 reports original gridworld training experiments comparing DReST and default agents, including learning curves, learned policies, lopsided rewards, and hyperparameter sensitivity results.

after.justification: v6 retains these original experimental results in Section 6 and Appendix E, including comparisons of agents’ USEFULNESS and NEUTRALITY.

M1.justification: The DReST reward function, normalization, grouping into meta-episodes, observations, and tabular REINFORCE procedure are unchanged. Renaming IPP to PAP does not introduce a method change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same example gridworld, lopsided-reward scenario, and Appendix E gridworld collection. No training or evaluation scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparisons remain DReST agents versus agents trained with the default reward function. Methods discussed as prior work or future comparators retain the same status.

E3.justification: Sections 4–6 and Appendix E retain the same metrics and experimental settings. For example, the main experiment still uses 131,072 mini-episodes, lambda = 0.9, gamma = 0.95, and the same learning-rate and exploration schedules.

E4.justification: The lopsided-reward test, lambda/meta-episode-size sensitivity analysis in Figure 7, and learned-policy case studies in Figures 9–16 are retained without changes to their questions or evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same ten-agent comparisons, the 10th–90th percentile bands in Figure 6, and eight agents per hyperparameter combination with one-standard-deviation bands in Figure 7.

E6.justification: The numerical plots, learned-policy images, and reported findings match; all embedded figure images are identical. This includes DReST agents’ high NEUTRALITY and both agent types’ failure to collect C3 in the Hidden Treasure gridworld.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, and proofs in Appendices A–D are unchanged, including the POST/POSL reasoning, ILPACS and shutdownability arguments, Theorem 5.1, and Lemma D.2.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that DReST trains simple agents to be USEFUL and NEUTRAL, offers initial evidence toward shutdownable advanced agents, and incurs a small shutdownability tax in the tested setting. The proposal’s renaming does not change these claims.

C2.justification: Sections 7–8 retain the same mechanism explanations and qualifications concerning advanced agents, stochastic environments, neural networks, and misalignment. Appendix E retains the same interpretations of training instability and gridworld failures.

D1.justification: The observation encoding, reward implementation, hyperparameters, training schedules, and reward-clipping details remain unchanged. No implementation or resource-access information is added or removed, and hyperlink targets match.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning relative to earlier research are unchanged. The renamed proposal remains attributed to Thornley (2024b), with the same explanation of its relationship to existing shutdown approaches.

P1.justification: “Incomplete Preferences Proposal (IPP)” becomes “POST-Agents Proposal (PAP)” in the abstract, introduction, and related work. The first-page notice changes from “Preprint. Under review.” to publication at TAIS Conference 2025; the remaining prose and section order are retained.

P2.justification: Text reflows across columns and pages, shifting the discussion opening, conclusion ending, references, and appendix material. The two-column design, figures, captions, and table structure are retained.

improvement.justification: v6 updates the proposal’s name and publication notice and changes pagination, while retaining the same method, experimental evidence, theoretical arguments, and limitations. These editorial changes establish no meaningful net difference in the paper’s overall quality.
